answer: In an agent economy, each identity must bond a refundable stake before it can transact. Spawning a new agent is cheap, but every voyage into the marketplace demands fresh locked collateral, so a Sybil attacker who spins up a mesa of fake agents must separately fund each one. Misbehavior triggers slashing, so the attackers bonded atlas of personas becomes pure liability: N fakes cost N stakes, and collusion only multiplies capital at risk rather than influence gained.
